findings.title: Numerical equality is labeled bitwise replay
findings.finding: The token, full-logit and portable-next-step checks use torch.equal. exact() checks tensor dtype and shape, then torch.equal; its scalar branch uses Python equality. torch.equal treats floating +0 and -0 as equal, whereas their byte representations differ. Direct token/logit checks also lack an explicit dtype comparison. The emitted *_bitwise_* flags therefore assert a stronger check than the implementation performs.
findings.impact: No actual replay difference or changed prediction was observed because numerical execution was prohibited. This is a concrete qualification-claim defect, not evidence that default Adam training is wrong. A root release requiring literal floating bit identity cannot rely on these checks as written.
findings.required_resolution: Use a dtype/shape/layout check and flattened contiguous uint8 byte-view comparisons for floating tensors (following the already sealed v4 comparator), with a byte-aware scalar policy where needed; alternatively issue a reviewed successor that explicitly narrows the release/design/receipt guarantee to exact numerical equality.
findings.launch_scope: Blocks literal bitwise qualification as currently required; does not independently demonstrate that the bounded fit cannot run or that TEST is used.

findings.title: Full Adam Python state is broader than the portable checkpoint
findings.finding: Portable state stores optimizer.state_dict(), then restores it with optimizer.load_state_dict(). This captures numerical Adam state and parameter-group primitive options, not the complete optimizer Python __dict__ such as defaults, hook registries and internal runtime flags. The comparison helper compares the same state_dict projection. The live joint deepcopy is broader, but the portable format is not.
findings.impact: The runner constructs ordinary source Adam, adds no hooks or scheduler and does not change defaults, so there is no demonstrated next-step or numerical-state error in this admitted scope. The full-Python-state wording should not become a reusable arbitrary-optimizer closure claim.
findings.required_resolution: Describe the checkpoint as complete numerical/default-Adam state_dict plus the separately saved model/RNG/gradient/config scope, or explicitly inventory and serialize any additional mutable Python fields that the intended stronger guarantee needs.
findings.launch_scope: Nonblocking scope clarification for the present default-Adam driver.

assessment: One literal bitwise-qualification mismatch and one nonblocking optimizer-state scope overclaim were identified. No accidental TEST scoring, wrong official columns, recipe-value mismatch, default-Adam group-rule mismatch, checkpoint-selection error, or concrete numerical/replay failure was found at source level. Actual official-data and GPU/runtime/resource evidence remains unexecuted and unqualified by this review.
